paper.title: Tables of 64-bit Mersenne Twisters
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Modeling and Computer Simulation 10(4)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the paper's recurrence (n=312, m=156, r=31, twist constant b5026f5aa96619e9) and tempering; the init_by_array64 seeding was re-implemented from the authors' reference source, which defines its multipliers; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: after init_by_array64({0x12345, 0x23456, 0x34567, 0x45678}) the first 1000 outputs of the 64-bit generator equal the 1000 values the authors published
a default-seeded (5489) mt19937_64 produces 9981545732273789042 as its 10000th output, the value the C++ standard requires

expected_values_source.what: the 1000 genrand64_int64() outputs in the authors' mt19937-64.out.txt; the 10000th-output value from the C++ standard draft ([rand.predef], mt19937_64)
expected_values_source.note: the values are data, copied as numbers; the authors' code was read only to confirm the seeding constants and was not copied. The 10000th-output value comes from the C++ standard, not from the 2000 paper.

negative_control: built with -DMT_M=155 (middle offset 155 instead of 156), 0 of 1000 published outputs match, the 10000th-output check fails and the program exits 1 (checked on ounce-core Tier-3 and natively)
not_checked: the paper's period and equidistribution tables, and the other Mersenne exponents it tabulates (only the 2^19937-1 member is run)
the real-valued outputs (genrand64_real*), which the authors' .out file also lists
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 1000 published MT19937-64 outputs and the standard's 10000th value. It does not show the statistical claims hold.
